highlightAliases.new: Hyperprolactinemia tiers: mild 20–50 ng/mL (rarely needs treatment, review medicines, renal function and TSH and repeat a mild elevation after rest), moderate 50–250 ng/mL (refer — likely prolactinoma), severe >250 ng/mL (refer — almost always a large prolactinoma) (p1525, p1528).

highlightAliases.new: Primary hyperaldosteronism affects 5–10% of hypertensive patients; workup = plasma aldosterone:renin ratio, withdraw spironolactone for 4 weeks before testing when safe and feasible; primary hyperaldosteronism suggested by aldosterone >10 ng/dL with renin activity <1 ng/mL/hr (p1532–1533).

highlightAliases.old: Exam traps: the chapter gives two different vitamin D deficiency thresholds in the same section — AGS <30 ng/mL vs IOM <12 ng/mL (insufficiency 12–20) (p1539) — know which guideline a question is citing.
highlightAliases.new: Exam traps: the historical AGS fall-prevention goal in high-risk patients was a minimum of 30 ng/mL. Falling short of that goal does not itself diagnose vitamin D deficiency. The IOM classified values below 12 ng/mL as deficient (p1539) — know which guideline a question is citing.
